title: Observability playbook for on-demand analytics backfill tracing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: When we run on-demand backfills of usage analytics (reprocessing historical message batches or replaying ingest windows) we currently see noisy, misleading traces and SLIs because: traces are duplicated, ingest request IDs collide, synthetic probes are mixed with replayed traffic, and downstream aggregation windows produce transient SLO violations. This ticket is to author and validate an operational playbook + automation for safely running backfills with correct tracing and SLI hygiene so that teams can reprocess data without polluting long-term SLO dashboards or alerting.
acceptance_criteria: A concise runbook exists that lists safe backfill preconditions and step-by-step commands for the analytics pipeline
Backfill job wrapper attaches a deterministic "replay_id" header and isolates traces in the tracing UI (tagging and a saved filter)
Synthetic probes and canary traffic are excluded from replay windows automatically (via flagging or tenant isolation)
Dashboards and alerting rules have temporary scoped suppression during the replay with automated rollback after verification
End-to-end verification checklist and a test backfill with no lasting SLI drift recorded in the golden SLI history
runbook_steps: Validate target partitions and snapshot job plan (size, time range, estimated tokens)
Generate a unique replay_id and record it in Jira + Slack channel for audit
Kick off read-only replay with header 'X-Replay-Run: <replay_id>' and 'X-Trace-Isolated: true'
Activate tracing filter for 'replay_id' in the tracing UI and create a temporary dashboard slice
Enable scoped alert suppression: create a short-lived suppression token that excludes alerts for affected SLIs and tag with 'replay:<replay_id>'
Monitor synthetic-probe signals and ensure probe-run timestamps do not overlap replay windows; pause probes if overlap detected
Observe a dry-run in staging with identical topology; confirm no SLI regressions in staging before production
After replay completes, run reconciliation job to de-duplicate events and mark processed ids as 'replayed' in the ingestion index
Run verification queries from the acceptance checklist and sign off in the ticket; remove suppression token and verify alerts resume
Archive replay metadata (replay_id, operator, job manifest, link to PRs) to the replay registry for future audits
implementation_notes: We will implement a small middleware in the backfill runner that injects two headers: X-Replay-Run and X-Trace-Isolated; downstream services must copy these into trace/span tags
Tracing UI needs a saved filter and a link-generating endpoint; proposal PR: github.com/redwood/replay-tracing-ux/pull/12
Suppression will use the existing alerting API but scoped to a tag 'replay:<replay_id>' to avoid broad noisier suppression
Reconciliation de-dup will re-use the dedupe_shard job with an added replay_id allowlist to avoid reprocessing legitimate duplicates
We must update ingest SDK docs and console runbook pages (Confluence) with examples and CLI snippets

qa_plan: Create a synthetic dataset with controlled duplicates and run a staged backfill; confirm dedupe and trace isolation
Run smoke queries comparing pre-backfill and post-backfill SLI baselines over a 24h window
Verify alerting suppression is applied only for the replay_id tag and that normal alerts resume after suppression removal
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Suppression accidentally muting unrelated alerts — Mitigation: scope suppression to 'replay:<id>' tag and require two-person approval for production suppression
Risk: Traces from replays pollute long-term trace store and increase cost — Mitigation: TTL shorter for replay-tagged traces and optional export suppression
Risk: Replayed messages reintroduce client-visible duplicates — Mitigation: reconciliation job marks ids and downstream idempotency checks enforced
